page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor. Featuring an x86_64 architecture operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, the configuration supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. Memory capacity is provisioned at 128.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio typical of compute-intensive profiles. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is present via AES and SHA-NI instruction sets alongside AVX, BMI2, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

Hardware resource distribution reflects a pure compute node design without integrated local instance storage and lacking specialized accelerator hardware such as GPUs. Network throughput is bounded by a baseline bandwidth limit of 16 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are attached by default. External cloud storage is required for persistent disk operations.

Benchmark evaluations reveal substantial aggregate compute and encryption throughput balanced against modest per-thread execution speed. The instance achieved top-quartile results in PassMark overall CPU tests (52514.65), PassMark CPU encryption (68034.72), Geekbench ray tracing (55013.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (251.92 GB/sec). Conversely, single-thread stress-ng throughput placed in the bottom 10 percent (767.59) and single-threaded gzip compression scored in the lower quartile, demonstrating that the instance relies on wide parallelization across its 64 vCPUs rather than single-core frequency to deliver compute density.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high vCPU allocation provides economical multi-core computing capacity for parallel batch jobs and compile-heavy workloads. The primary tradeoff lies in the lower single-core throughput and the absence of bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures. The instance is well matched for Clang code compilation, multithreaded data compression, parallel computational simulations, batch processing, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at 2.6 GHz on the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores and 128.0 GB of system memory, delivering a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio suited for CPU-heavy tasks. The instance includes 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and does not feature GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the platform demonstrates strong multi-core computational throughput, excelling in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and encryption workloads, while displaying modest single-thread speed. Cost efficiency is characterized by dense core allocation for parallel tasks rather than peak per-thread performance. The instance is recommended for software compilation, encryption processing, parallel data transformation, and multi-threaded batch services.
